claim: On host macos-m5pro-20260924 (Apple M5 Pro, Mac17,8, 18 cores, 24 GB; macOS 26.5.1 build 25F80, arm64) the adaptive-paper lane ran in an isolated, hash-locked CPython 3.12.14 runtime (nautilus-trader 2.0.0rc5, alpaca-py 0.44.0, numpy 2.5.3, pandas 3.0.6; 20 packages from evidence/artifacts/macos-syn-e2e-20260924/requirements-macos-arm64-py312.lock). With the real NautilusTrader LiveNode engine it passed 732 adaptive-paper tests (one skip by design), 17 native-faults offline tests, 28 market-research tests, the mover synthetic trial (evidence class SYN: 2 entries, 2 X2 exits, 4 native fills, flat, cash reconciled) and the synthetic capacity fixture (180 submissions and native fills, flat, reconciled). Every run used local synthetic ports and zero broker connections.
limitations: local_integration only: the real NautilusTrader 2.0.0rc5 engine ran against this repository's synthetic broker ports and fixtures. No Alpaca or IBKR connection, credential, market data or study data was used; this is not paper or live broker acceptance. The mover SYN fills and P&L come from mover_runner.synthetic_path's scripted prices on invented tickers (evidence/artifacts/macos-syn-e2e-20260924/mover-synthetic-scan.json) and are not outcomes.

Recorded outside Claude Code's Seatbelt sandbox, which denies the loopback bind (EPERM) that 3 test_adaptive_paper_metrics HTTP-server tests need. Inside the sandbox the same adaptive-paper command ran 732 tests with exactly those 3 errors and 1 skip, and the other suites and both synthetic runs passed there (evidence/artifacts/macos-syn-e2e-20260924/summary.json).

The one skip is by design: exchange_calendars is not in the pinned lane runtime (test_adaptive_paper_sessions). Not run here: the mover-early-entry study tests, the live native-faults harness, the full repository suite in this runtime and the 42 unchanged upstream adapter tests.

The trading-nautilus adoption profile lists bwrap, which macOS lacks, so the network-namespaced engine replay of blueprints/us-equities/engine-nautilus is not covered. No hardware_profile.py --record-host entry exists for this host (no hardware_profile_ref); it has 24 GB, not the 64 GB of the macOS host projected in docs/next-host-stages.md.
